Daily Devotional

October 28

6 Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded. 7 Unto you therefore which believe he is precious: but unto them which be disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner, - 1 Peter 2:6-7 (KJV)

 Peter has been telling us to be living stones of the house that Jesus is the corner stone of. This verse is quoting from Old Testament scripture (Isaiah 28:16), and it always points to Jesus as being the corner stone of the church building, where the ones that believe in Jesus are the building itself. This same point is used elsewhere in the New Testament (Romans 9:33), always with Jesus as the corner stone, and those that believe on Him as not being ashamed (confounded) (Romans 10:11).

 If you have been born again, and made Jesus as your Lord and Savior (Romans 10:9-10), then you will believe that He is precious, as He was God in the flesh (1 Timothy 3:16), and our God is most precious. Elsewhere in scripture the word translated “disallowed” here, was translated “rejected”, so this is saying that those that reject Jesus as their Savior, have rejected the very cornerstone of the Church. Jesus used this same term when He was talking with the Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 21:42, Mark 12:10), and referred to Himself as being the cornerstone of the New Testament Church. Peter goes on to talk about Jesus being the stumbling stone and rock of offence to those who stumble at the Word (Romans 2:8), but calls those that believe a chosen generation, royal priesthood and holy nation (Romans 2:9) – Wow, to think that we, who believe, are all those things. The last thing he says is we are a peculiar people, and I can relate to that one for sure. Praise God for loving us peculiar people.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com

Despite the icy temperature he kept his house at, he found himself covered in sweat. Glancing down at his naked body, he found that he had no covers. He looked over and say why: Maria lay there, curled up with all the blanket.

Then his thoughts turned to why he’d woken up. The dream was fading away now, but he remembered a single face he’d only seen once before: Luke Degras.

They’d met the one time and spent a long time arguing over this and that before Steiner finally slammed the door shut and walked way. By all rights, he should have informed the police that a wanted war criminal had been at his door and had offered to talk politics. Thought the meeting had happened nearly have a year ago, something about it just… bothered Steiner, not in a way he could put his finger to, but in a way that made him stop and dwell thereupon for short periods of time before forgetting thereabout utterly until he next recalled it.

He slid his legs over the side of the bed and got up. Steiner felt his dry throat crying out to be watered. He mosied on over to the kitchen and found himself a glass and filled it from the tap.

Leaning over the island countertop in the center of the kitchen, he gazed out at nothing in particular. He just drank his water and contemplated making breakfast.

Luke came into his head again. "I gave up my dream because I thought I was not worthy to have it., he’d said. I retook my dream but I molded it. I molded it to fit what I believed!

The thought was odd to Steiner. Luke had been of the view that while the Iron Dream had its power, that it would be the death of Germany. As bellicose as he was , Steiner had to concede that the whole world would be against the Fatherland if… no, when he succeeded. His mind turned to the ten principles of National Socialism, then to the words of the Southern under whom Steiner had worked when we was a mercenary

“National Socialism had its time, and while it was respectable, it was a product of its ery German time,” the man had said in his honeyed Southern accent that Steiner tried his best to emulate when he attempted to speak the language.

Steiner had rejected that idea. The Iron Dream was true. It was a part of Steiner’s very soul.

So how come when he thought about everything in context, he felt like something was wrong. Something didn’t add up. Like he wasn’t being honest with himself. That just didn’t work, especially not when the first principle of National Socialism was “BE HONEST”.

“A National Socialist faces a fact whether he likes it or not. Dishonesty is the mark of the enemy. National Socialism above all represents living truth in its purest form.” Or so the principle went.

He heard Maria enter the kitchen before he saw her. She’d found her panties but that was about it. Under more lecherous times, he might have paused to enjoy the sight. As it was, he gave her a noncommittal nod to let her know that he was aware of her.

“Steiner?” she asked, rubbing her eyes. She sounded tired. A part of him wondered how she could walk after last night. He drank more water to keep himself from grinning. What was he, fourteen? God’s sake, he was turning thirty-three in a month. “What are you doing up?”

He shrugged.

“Come back to bed. It’s too cold to be out.” She hugged herself with her arms, giving a little shiver.

Steiner refilled his glass from the water filter. He didn’t bother to reply.

“Steiner,” Maria moaned with a frown.

He gave her an appraising look, thinking her over. “Maria,” he said at length. “What do you think of National Socialism?”

She blinked before uttering a low groan. “It’s too early for that. Come back to bed.”

Steiner raised a brow.

“I swear,” she said, shaking her head, “with you it’s always politics, business, or trying to remove my panties. Can’t we ever just be normal?”

“Nope,” he said. “Gimme an answer.”

“I dunno,” Maria sighed, leaning against a wall. “It’s hard. Odd. too extreme. But you make it work, I guess, and people love you.”

“Do you think people would respond to a rebranding thereof?” he asked her quite seriously.

She rolled her sleepy eyes.

“I mean, you know me. I always do what I feel is right or otherwise necessary.” He finished his glass of water. “And.. I don’t know, I have this feeling maybe… I don’t know, that…” As great as National Socialism was, it was a product of a different era for different problems than those we face today. He couldn’t finish. It sounded silly when he put it like that, and Maria was giving him a funny look.

“What are you going on about?” she asked, squinting at him.

“Well, do you think the Iron Dream needs a fresh coat of paint? A new set of wheels.? New arms to fight for today?’

She tilted her head. “Was that water or was that vodka? You’re talking all sorts of weird.”

Steiner shook his head. Then, after a moment’s thought, he said in a singsong, “Answer me and I’ll make your breakfast.”

He smiled. “Because you’re cute when you act like a woman.”

Steiner did not come with her. For the rest of the night, he stood there in his kitchen, mulling things over.

I have a computer science degree, and can say that you'd want to use SI units almost all of the time. Usage of Imperial units should be discouraged except in very special cases. When you're using Imperial units you end up running into conversion factors between inches, feet, and miles. Think about going from inches to feet. You have to divide by 12, and figure out how many inches are left from the remainder. That's nuts. You'll end up wasting processor cycles just to make your output human readable. If you're using SI units then converting from centimeters, meters, and kilometers is just a matter of division or multiplication. Additionally, if you're moving between measurement systems you'll always end up loosing some precision when you do a conversion. Decimal places are handy, but they're only approximations. If you're wanting to have good accuracy then you need to use actual fractions, and you're going to run into a whole other mess of issues getting that to work properly.
Tl;DR when converting you quickly get tangled in a mess of fractions and magic.
